source.title: The relationship between symbolic play and language acquisition: A meta-analytic review

confidence_rationale: Best quantitative summary of the play-language association: 35 studies, a robust small-to-medium correlation (reported r ~ .35) holding across ages 1-6, comprehension vs production, and concurrent vs longitudinal designs. It supports the tracking half of MECH-308 but is correlational only, and r ~ .35 leaves most language variance unexplained by play. Held near 0.5 because the claim asserts language is instantiated within play, which a moderate correlation cannot distinguish from a shared symbolic-capacity or shared-environment cause.
failure_signatures: A shared third factor (general symbolic/representational capacity, nonverbal IQ, caregiver input) can produce the play-language correlation without play being the substrate of language.
Symbolic play measures often include verbal components or adult modelling, inflating the association.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Across 35 studies, symbolic play and language are associated at a small-to-medium magnitude that is stable across age (1-6 y), language modality and concurrent vs longitudinal design.
mapping.ree_translation: Direct but partial evidence for the MECH-308 prediction that language competence tracks play maturation (acceptance criterion A1, play half). The longitudinal component is the part closest to 'tracking' rather than co-occurrence.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Symbolic/pretend play is only one slice of MECH-308's play_mode (which also covers social-frame opening/closing, rough-and-tumble, basic-expression exchange). The meta-analysis does not compare play against motor or sensory milestones, so A1's specificity clause is untested here. Correlation, not the causal 'language is a play-game' assertion.
mapping.source_context: Meta-analysis of typically and atypically developing child samples; metadata verified via web search hits (ScienceDirect/Semantic Scholar/MPG listings); full text not retrieved in this session.

confidence_components.notes: Effect size and moderator pattern taken from retrieved abstract-level summaries, not the full text.
